correctness.rationale: The one-particle eigenspaces are the constant line T, the block-constant zero-sum space V and the sum U of the internal zero-sum spaces W_a. Their eigenvalues divided by J are m(q-1), -m and 0; the six symmetric pair sums are distinct for the stated q and J. Diagonal evaluation is injective on sectors with a T-factor. For n>=3, the diagonal map on the symmetric square of the n-site zero-sum space has rank n: the products of two distinct vectors e_i-e_n isolate the nth coordinate, and squares then give the others. At n=2 it has rank one. Thus the ranks on Sym^2 U and Sym^2 V are q r_m and q; on V times W_a it is the nonzero evaluation at block a times W_a, of rank m-1. These rank counts give the three dark dimensions. For projection norms, the diagonal kernel on n sites is contained in the off-diagonal pair space and is permutation invariant, so the same squared projector norm on every normalized distinct-site pair is its dimension divided by binom(n,2), namely (n-3)/(n-1) for n>=3 (zero for n=2). In the cross-part case the U-only survival weight is (m-1)^2/m^2, the two orthogonal mixed terms together contribute 2(m-1)(q-2)/[m^2(q-1)], and the collective term contributes (q-3)/[m^2(q-1)]. In the same part, each V component is in the direction of the block evaluation functional, so neither sector involving V survives; the internal kernel gives the piecewise formula. Doublons have zero dark projection. The loss operator annihilates the dark space and its orthogonal complement is invariant. Any eigenvector on that complement has strictly negative imaginary eigenvalue, by taking the imaginary part of its own energy expectation and using the positive rates. Finite dimension then gives decay, even with Jordan blocks, and the stated survival for arbitrary density matrices. Independent symmetric-tensor kernels gave dimensions (3,3,0), (24,16,2), (33,9,0) in the three channels for (q,m)=(3,2),(4,3),(3,4); both capture probabilities matched in each case.
residual_risks: Requires q>=3, equal part sizes, uniform nonzero hopping, no coherent interactions or detunings, and strictly positive loss at every site. The numerical checks are bounded corroboration; the proof is asymptotic and does not estimate decay times.

evidence: The prior walk literature supplies degeneracy-protected non-detection and the noninteracting symmetric Hamiltonian; Everest–Hush–Lesanovsky instead use hard-core bosons and nonlocal loss.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General invariant-subspace principles supply a reduction, not the ranks of this family’s collision restrictions or the localized projection weights. The hard-core model removes the double-occupancy sector and does not dominate the onsite pair-loss problem.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: In the equal-weight star the hub leaves the leaf-zero-sum symmetric square after removing the other zero-energy factor by hub diagonal evaluation. Its diagonal kernel is the same block-space kernel that controls the collective term here, so that constituent alone is not a new kernel calculation. But even allowing unequal part sizes in the two-part result does not cover three parts: the symmetric pair-energy collision at q=2 disappears and there is no counterpart in either prior theorem to the mixed internal/collective V times U channel plus its capture contribution. The total projected weights and energy-resolved classification therefore do not follow by substitution or direct specialization.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md spectral ranks, localized projection laws and asymptotic loss
value.rationale: Collision monitoring of two indistinguishable walkers poses a concrete question beyond whether a graph has dark states: how much of a localized pair actually avoids loss, and in which spectral sectors? The balanced family separates three mechanisms with different dependence on part size and number of parts. The energy census and the two simple capture laws distinguish adjacent and nonadjacent pairs and identify a collective threshold at four parts; the effect cannot be read off from total dark dimension or from the two-part case. Rate independence also specifies exactly what robust asymptotic observable can be predicted under site-dependent positive loss.
residual_risks: No claim about finite-time losses, unequal parts, interactions, or nonuniform hopping.
